io.text: Each leaf descriptor carries contract `sbf.adapter/2`; no sampled output and no module of section 3 holds a schema name or key listed as foreign above.

`detect` and `scan` return what the exported detect and scan functions of their module return for the same arguments, and `scan` uses the detection it is given (null selects the not-detected result); `listReadSet` returns the `filesRead` of that scan, an empty list for a tree that is not detected; `diagnostics` returns one info entry.

A root that is undefined, null, a number, an empty string, a missing path, a file path, an array or an object gives `detect` null, the not-detected result, an empty read set and the not-detected diagnostic, and does not throw for these eight roots. A detection passed by hand that is an empty object, a string, an object with a numeric projectRoot or an object without packageFile makes `scan` and `listReadSet` throw TypeError; null selects the not-detected result.

`runScan` with one leaf and an empty terms list returns `sbf.scan-report/2` whose `related_modules`, `files_read` and `api_surface_source` equal `modules`, `filesRead` and `apiSurfaceSource` of the scan, and whose unknowns end with the `scanNotes`, after two notes that `runScan` adds.
No leaf id is an entry of the ADAPTERS list, and neither registry file names a path of this layer.

`HTTP_WAVE_BC_TARGETS` is a frozen array. `validateWaveBcCatalog` returns an empty list for it and throws TypeError, not an error text, for an array that holds null; this defect is recorded as a fixture of `BASELINE.json` and not repaired here.

identity.text: In the sampled scans `operationId` is null on each endpoint and `operationIds` is empty on each controller, so no operation identity is derived. `method` holds the handler name (null for an inline handler) and `verb` holds the HTTP method.

`className` is Hono(file relative to the project root:variable), KoaRouter(file basename:variable) or NextRoute(file relative to the project root). Two Koa router files of one basename in different folders get equal `className` values; the Hono and Next forms differ for them.

Registrations are not merged or renumbered. Two Hono or Koa calls with one verb and path stay two endpoints; written on one source line they share verb, path and `line` and differ only in `method`. In the sampled Next scans, two route files for one path that export a method in common stay two controllers and one scan note names both files, while two files for one path that export different methods give no such note.
`line` is the 1-based line of the registration (of the export in a Next file). Inserting one line above a route moves `line` by one and leaves `className`, `verb` and `path` as they were.

In the sampled scans `file` of a controller is the scan root as passed, joined with the path of the file below it: absolute for an absolute scan root and relative to the working directory for a relative one. `filesRead` entries are relative to the scan root in both cases. The file named in `className` is relative to the project root for Hono and Next but only a basename for Koa (`id-class-name`), and does not depend on the form of the scan root; for a project below the scan root these bases differ, which the sampled Hono project shows.

No sampled output has a key with hash, digest or sha as a word of its name, so the layer emits no identity digest. Each sampled endpoint has `verb`, `path` and `line`, and its controller has `className`; together they are a regression key within one scan and not a stable identifier: `line` moves when a line is inserted (`id-line`), and two registrations written on one source line carry equal values (`id-duplicate`).

unknown.text: In the sampled scans `entities`, `enums` and `dtos` are empty lists, written as the literal [] in the module sources; an empty list there means not extracted.

A tree the detector rejects gives `detect` null and a result with the keys `modules`, `filesRead` and `scanNotes` only, with one note; a detected tree without routes gives empty `modules` and a non-empty `filesRead`, so empty `modules` alone does not tell the two apart.

In the sampled Next scans a route file that exports a supported method and whose path cannot be built because of a segment emits no endpoint and one note naming the file and one of the five reason codes above; the same kind of file without a supported method gets no note, and a file withheld because the base path is unresolved gets a note that names the file and no reason code. In the sampled Hono and Koa scans no note names a reason code. A withheld form is reported as note text only, and no endpoint key carries a status or reason.

`parseHonoShowRoutes` returns `schema`, `routes` and `unknownLines`; indented lines bind as handlers to the route above them, a line it cannot read stays in `unknownLines` with its line number, and empty, null or missing input gives empty lists.

A short or empty endpoint list does not show that the source has no such route: the record holds fixtures in which a route form is lost without a note (`silent-drop`) or the router is not detected (`undetected-router`), so a consumer treats an absent route as unknown, not as absent.

promotion.text: Neither JSON file mentions contracts/next, so no gate for output in that form and no owner for such a gate is recorded; this RFC adds no gate and no owner.

ownership.text: The directories `python-litestar`, `python-starlette` and `scope` of this layer contain no file named adapter.mjs; the non-null `scope_record` values of `BASELINE.json` are paths inside these directories.
